title: Issue 1 Cover — The Weight of Dead Iron
summary: Sell Issue 1 as the first overwhelming resurfacing of a forgotten heroic age: Theo is tiny in the present-day trench while an immense, still-unreadable ancient presence coheres across stars, dust and volumetric light above him. The buried object is the physical trigger; the cosmic memory is the promise. Do not identify the figure as Starbreaker or reveal the battlefield.
settingText: Olyria-Prime excavation trench at shift end beneath an enormous night sky. Black bedrock, practical work lights and drill machinery remain small at the bottom of the composition. Above the trench, stars, dust and pale-gold volumetric cloud begin to suggest a colossal humanoid presence with no readable armor, face or faction identity.

panelPlan.text: SINGLE FULL-BLEED, HIGHLY STYLIZED COVER IMAGE. Use extreme vertical scale. Theo is a tiny dark present-day figure at the bottom of the trench beside the halted drill and one exposed manufactured black edge. The upper two-thirds belong to sky, stars, cosmic haze and the suggestion of impossible remembered scale.

A colossal ancient humanoid presence should be only partly legible in the sky: shoulder line, head silhouette, one arm or weapon-like axis implied through volumetric fog, starlight and pale-gold fracture. It must read as a resurfacing memory-image, not as a literal giant standing physically over Olyria.

Do not reveal Starbreaker's face, fractured armor language, chest motif or exact weapon. Before the reader meets him, the cover should promise that something godlike existed without telling them who or what side it belonged to.
Let the manufactured seam under the drill visually rhyme with one razor-straight cosmic fracture in the sky, linking buried matter and returning memory.
COLOR IDENTITY: charcoal-black trench, cold steel work light, deep star black, restrained pale gold and ion-white cosmic fracture. Avoid warm mining-world sepia.
TRADE DRESS: reserve clean upper negative space within the star field for the masthead while allowing the giant silhouette to pass behind it without compromising legibility.
THUMBNAIL READ: tiny human at bottom + impossible trench seam + enormous half-seen figure in the stars.
SPOILER CEILING: no identifiable Starbreaker, no Redlin, no ancient battlefield geography, no full Desert Marker silhouette, no memory-event action, no Rae archive evidence, no Adrian.

title: Issue 2 Cover — Glass Dust and Violet Light
summary: Sell Issue 2 as a mythic collision between two ancient heroic powers with coherent opposing solutions. Starbreaker and Redlin are immense memory-presences occupying opposite halves of the cosmic field, while General Mero is a nearly tiny human figure below them. The cover should feel like remembered gods arguing through force, not a conventional superhero duel.
settingText: Stylized remembered Desert Marker conflict suspended before irreversible catastrophe. Space, violet glass dust, ruined terrain and stellar haze merge into a mythic double-exposure field. Starbreaker and Redlin dominate at colossal scale; Mero and the battlefield are tiny beneath them.

panelPlan.text: SINGLE FULL-BLEED COSMIC CONFLICT COVER. Starbreaker and Redlin should be enormous, each too large to fit comfortably in frame. Use opposing diagonal masses rather than two standing full-body figures.

STARBREAKER side: white-gold fractured radiance, stellar rays, cutting directional force, crystalline energy seams and violent first-light geometry. REDLIN side: dense red-black containment, circular compression fields, deep crimson volumetric fog and enclosed force absorbing or restraining the same catastrophe.

The two figures may overlap in double exposure across stars and particulate glass dust. Their faces can be readable enough to establish character, but the image should feel like mythic memory rather than a literal scale diagram.

General Mero appears as one tiny human silhouette on the battlefield below, visually caught between impossible powers. His scale is essential: he is a human commander among beings remembered as larger than life.
The central conflict should be one shared unstable phenomenon caught between destruction and containment. Do not make them simply fire weapons at one another.
COLOR IDENTITY: hard white/gold on one side, deep red/black on the other, violet glass-dust transition through the center.
TRADE DRESS: masthead floats in controlled star-dark negative space above the conflict, preserving Issue 1 geometry.
THUMBNAIL READ: giant white-gold god versus giant red-black god, tiny human below.
SPOILER CEILING: no decisive detonation, no casualty aftermath, no Theo/Rae ancient identity, no later champions, no Reset.

title: Issue 3 Cover — The Architecture of Ruin
summary: Sell Issue 3 at civilization scale: the modern city is tiny beneath the resurfacing memory of Atlas, whose colossal blue-black-gold form seems to hold architecture, gravity and a buried dreadnought together across the sky. Present-day people and Vael-Tor remain small silhouettes below. The ancient figure is memory iconography, not literally present.
settingText: Rain-soaked Vael-Tor beneath a vast storm-dark sky. Contemporary city geometry and the buried black dreadnought break through one another below while an immense Atlas presence forms through cloud, rain, orbital light and deep blue-black cosmic mass overhead.

panelPlan.text: SINGLE FULL-BLEED MONUMENTAL COVER. Make Atlas the dominant visual event: colossal shoulders and arms spanning the upper field, his deep blue-black form built from storm cloud, star-dark mass and restrained gold gravity/orbital geometry.

Atlas should appear to be bearing the whole visual weight of the image—city, hull, rain and fractured architecture seeming to hang within his gravity field. This is symbolic memory scale, not literal present-day physical size.

Below him, Vael-Tor and the resurfacing dreadnought form a compact band of modern architecture. Theo, Rae, Adrian, refugees and commuters may be reduced to small silhouettes or simplified human marks; do not require face-level realism at cover scale.

The dreadnought remains physically real and embedded in the city, but it should not compete with Atlas for primary dominance. The cover's promise is that the forgotten war was large enough to reshape worlds.
Use rain streaks, gravity arcs and low cloud as a double-exposure bridge between Atlas and the architecture.
COLOR IDENTITY: saturated deep blue-black, cold rain cyan, restrained gold gravity lines, black hull. Avoid muddy gray.
THUMBNAIL READ: gigantic Atlas-shaped sky mass over a tiny modern city split by ancient war architecture.
SPOILER CEILING: no fully operational dreadnought, no ancient Theo/Rae, no later identity reveal, no Reset imagery.

title: Issue 4 Cover — Silence in the Vault
summary: Sell Issue 4 as remembered judgment at impossible scale. Arbiter should loom like a civilization-sized tribunal above and through Pax-Aeterna, while the black treaty table and tiny present trio sit far below. The image promises that a forgotten decision once carried extinction-level weight without revealing Theo or Rae's ancient roles.
settingText: Pax-Aeterna under a severe black-and-silver sky treatment. The present treaty vault and long black table occupy the lower field. Above and behind the architecture, Arbiter's colossal judicial silhouette forms through hard geometric light, dark cloud, silver fracture and restrained gold lines.

panelPlan.text: SINGLE FULL-BLEED JUDGMENT COVER. Arbiter dominates the upper two-thirds at colossal symbolic scale. Her severe vertical head structure, pale/dark judicial armor and hard geometric silhouette should read like a living verdict written across the sky.
The black treaty table begins near the bottom edge and points toward the tiny present-day Theo, Rae and Adrian at the far end, making human scale almost incidental beneath the returning memory.

Use dual exposure so evacuation lights, departing vessels or distant civilian movement faintly occupy Arbiter's lower silhouette and the vault openings. The cover should imply that judgment was made while real lives moved beneath it.
Do not depict ancient Theo or ancient Rae anywhere in the memory layer. Their historical participation remains unrevealed at cover-open time.
COLOR IDENTITY: black, silver-white, severe pale stone and restrained judicial gold; optional deep red edge light from the ancient conflict, never enough to make Arbiter read demonic.
Use lightning-like hard geometric fissures rather than soft mystical glow. Arbiter should feel precise, terrifyingly controlled and larger than the room that remembers her.
THUMBNAIL READ: immense judicial goddess silhouette + long black table + three tiny figures.
SPOILER CEILING: no ancient Theo/Rae, no explicit extinction event, no midpoint identity reveal, no Reset.

title: Issue 5 Cover — Embers of the Zenith
summary: Sell Issue 5 as personal identity swallowed by mythic recovered history. Theo and Rae remain small present-day silhouettes while colossal ancient presences and aligned double exposures reveal that they were inside the heroic age, not merely watching it. Afterlight supplies the issue's luminous restorative color identity.
settingText: Highly stylized convergence of present architecture and ancient remembered space. Theo and Rae stand small in the lower foreground. Above them, ancient memory expands to cosmic scale: Mero and Arbiter as monumental institutional presences on opposing sides, Afterlight's living white-gold restoration burning through the center.

panelPlan.text: SINGLE FULL-BLEED DUAL-EXPOSURE COVER. Present Theo and Rae are small, separate foreground silhouettes. Behind and above each, their ancient human positions align in much larger transparent memory layers—Theo near Mero, Rae near Arbiter—but do not make ancient Theo or Rae themselves god-sized or divine.

Mero and Arbiter may occupy monumental upper-side presences representing the institutions Theo and Rae served: Mero human but mythically enlarged by memory on one side, Arbiter truly colossal and severe on the other.

Afterlight should cross the composition as luminous white-gold living restoration: seed-like structures, translucent botanical geometry, regenerative rays and glowing volumetric haze. She may be a giant distant figure in the upper center, distinct from Starbreaker's weaponized light.
The key visual idea is that the present silhouettes fit exactly into old positions inside a history that is vastly larger than their current lives.

COLOR IDENTITY: white-gold Afterlight luminosity against cooler charcoal/blue present silhouettes, with pale judicial geometry around Arbiter. Allow warm ember highlights without turning the whole image orange.
THUMBNAIL READ: two tiny modern figures below enormous overlapping ancient identities and restorative cosmic light.
SPOILER CEILING: do not reveal Theo's missing opinion to Mero, Rae's unfinished answer to Arbiter, the Reset choice, or finale positions.

title: Issue 6 Cover — The Margin of Error
summary: Sell Issue 6 as reality itself becoming uncertain under the resurfacing memory of Flux. Flux should dominate the cover as an enormous black-violet multiplied presence across sky and architecture, while present-day humans are tiny silhouettes inside a world whose possible histories no longer agree.
settingText: Present-day transit architecture reduced to a dark lower band beneath a vast violet-black cosmic probability field. Repeated rails, windows and star lines split into offset continuities while Flux appears as several overlapping colossal silhouettes that never fully resolve into one position.

panelPlan.text: SINGLE FULL-BLEED PROBABILITY COVER. Flux owns most of the image: one primary colossal readable form plus two or three offset giant silhouettes, all sharing a face/body identity but displaced in angle, opacity and position.
Use black-violet volumetric fog, prismatic seams, cosmic rays, doubled stars and misregistered architecture. The effect should feel like remembered reality branching, not generic purple magic.

Present-day Theo, Rae and one ordinary transit worker are tiny silhouettes along the bottom or lower-middle band. The worker may turn toward an impossible empty place/person-shape; keep human detail minimal and graphic.
Let rail lines, platform edges and star trails repeat into mutually incompatible vanishing points, visually extending Flux's uncertainty through the whole world.
COLOR IDENTITY: saturated violet, ultraviolet blue, black, occasional ion-white prismatic flare. Avoid magenta fantasy smoke.
TRADE DRESS: masthead can sit over a controlled dark-violet sky field while offset Flux contours pass behind it.
THUMBNAIL READ: one giant figure becoming several across violet-black space, tiny humans trapped below.
SPOILER CEILING: no explanation for Flux's disappearance, no Oryon, no Neo-Vectra policy resolution, no Reset mechanism.

title: Issue 7 Cover — Gravity and Consequence
summary: Sell Issue 7 as the return of ancient predictive power reproducing itself as modern control. Oryon should loom at colossal scale over Neo-Vectra in pale geometric light while Atlas stands as an opposing giant mass across the sky. Rae and the separated present-day couple are tiny silhouettes below the cosmic argument.
settingText: Neo-Vectra under a stylized night sky transformed by resurfacing memory. A temporary modern barrier crosses the lower foreground. Above it, Oryon's immense pale predictive geometry fills one side of the heavens while Atlas's deep blue-black-gold mass opposes him across the other.

panelPlan.text: SINGLE FULL-BLEED TWO-POWER COVER. Oryon dominates one upper side at giant scale: lean pale silhouette, severe face partly obscured by volumetric white/cool light, precise orbital lattices and predictive route geometry radiating from him across the city.

Atlas occupies the opposing upper field as a colossal blue-black-gold mass resisting that imposed geometry, his body language protective and gravitational rather than aggressive. Their conflict is ideological and spatial, not a laser duel.

Below them, Rae stands as a small dark silhouette near the temporary barrier. The recurring present-day couple appears on opposite sides of the divider, simplified enough to read graphically at thumbnail scale.
Let Oryon's predictive lines descend from the sky and become the same visual language as the modern barrier/grid below, making the rhyme between ancient prevention and present control immediate.
Use selective lightning-like geometry or orbital beam paths to create enormous energy without implying magical spellcasting.
COLOR IDENTITY: pale silver-white and cool cyan geometry versus Atlas blue-black mass and restrained gold; small neutral modern silhouettes below.
THUMBNAIL READ: two enormous opposing god-figures in the sky + tiny human barrier consequence below.
SPOILER CEILING: do not show Rae dismantling the policy, Adrian's temporary-measures admission, Kyn, the Core-Forge, or the finale choice.

title: Issue 8 Cover — The Shape of Tomorrow
summary: Sell the finale as full mythic convergence. Theo, Rae and Adrian are tiny present-day figures at the Reset scar while Kyn emerges as an immense empathic presence across the stars and the previously revealed heroic powers gather as colossal, partially obscured memory silhouettes around the composition. The cover promises civilization-scale choice without revealing the decision.
settingText: Core-Forge convergence rendered as present architecture at the bottom of an immense cosmic-memory field. The physical scar sits below. Above it, Kyn's vast gray-blue/white-teal-gold presence forms through stars, neural branching light and volumetric haze, with selected previously revealed champions appearing as enormous partial silhouettes at the edges.

panelPlan.text: SINGLE FULL-BLEED FINALE COVER. Theo, Rae and Adrian are very small present-day silhouettes around the physical scar in the lower 15–20 percent. Their triangle establishes the human decision point, but they should not dominate the image.

Kyn is the central colossal presence across the upper field: cool gray-blue skin, white/silver hair, white-teal-gold organic neural branching and immense translucent scale. Kyn should feel omnipresent through memory and empathy, not saintly, religious or literally giant in the present.

At the far edges and deeper layers, allow partially obscured colossal silhouettes or energy signatures of already revealed champions—Starbreaker white-gold fracture, Redlin crimson containment, Atlas deep blue mass, Arbiter hard judicial geometry, Afterlight living gold, Flux violet offset, Oryon pale lattice. Do not make a clean lineup; they should feel like all of the recovered war pressing into one image.
Use dual exposure between ancient foundations, star fields, volumetric fog and the Core-Forge geometry so past and present are no longer cleanly separable.
The scar itself must remain materially simple and non-mechanical. Do not invent a glowing Reset machine. Cosmic rays and converging light may point toward it without turning it into a device.
COLOR IDENTITY: teal-white-gold Kyn center with controlled spectral echoes of the season's prior issue colors around the perimeter, all grounded by deep black space.
THUMBNAIL READ: three tiny humans beneath one vast empathic cosmic presence, surrounded by the pressure of an entire forgotten pantheon.
SPOILER CEILING: no final interruption, no completed Reset/restoration action, no aftermath, no missing-stars image, no Regent reveal, no Season 2 explanation.
